title: Affine derived algebra-valued Hom with evaluation counit
statement: Let f:X -> Y be an affine morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Let A=f_*O_X and g:(X,O_X) -> (Y,A) be the direct-image algebra construction [def-sc-direct-image-algebra-derived-category]. Assume the derived categories D(O_Y) and D(A) [def-pc-derived-category] exist in the specified universes. Write rho:D(A) -> D(O_Y) for the chosen right derived functor of scalar restriction along O_Y -> A. Then there exist H:D(O_Y) -> D(A), an adjunction adjH:rho ⊣ H, and a natural isomorphism iota:RHom(O_Y,-) ≅ Id [def-pur-derived-internal-hom], such that for every K in D(O_Y) there is an isomorphism d:rho(H(K)) ≅ RHom(A,K) satisfying d.hom followed by RHom(O_Y -> A,K) followed by iota_K = adjH.counit_K. Here A in the Hom formula is the degree-zero O_Y-module f_*O_X, and O_Y -> A is the canonical unit-to-pushforward-unit morphism. No boundedness or quasi-coherence is required of K.

source.place: Tags 0BUZ, 0BV0 and 0AX3: derived scalar adjunction and evaluation counit

proof.text: Use [lem-sc-finite-sheafhom-affine-adjoint] to obtain the derived algebra-valued sheaf-Hom adjunction. Exact scalar restriction preserves quasi-isomorphisms; uniqueness of derived functors identifies its displayed L with the chosen rightDerivedFunctor rho. Transport the adjunction to obtain H and adjH.

Compute H on a functorial K-injective resolution of K. After scalar restriction it is the Hom complex from A[0]. The underlying module of A is canonically f_*O_X by the identity on sections. The localization comparison in [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] yields d. In each degree Hom(O_Y,I) identifies with I by evaluation at one; these maps commute with differential and restrictions. Localize this natural isomorphism, and compose with the inverse of the resolution quasi-isomorphism, obtaining iota.

Precomposition by O_Y -> A and evaluation at one is the chain map evaluating Hom(A,I) at one. The derived counit formula in [lem-sc-finite-sheafhom-affine-adjoint] descends this very map. Compatibility of the localization comparisons yields the required counit equality for every K.
